item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Compatible and structure-preserving discretizations of Hamiltonian PDE systems (Univ. TRENTO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-18 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-05 Analisi numerica

The objective of this research project is to develop new compatible and structure-preserving schemes for Hamiltonian PDE systems that originate from the SHTC / GENERIC frameworks. The new methods should discretize the original Lie-Poisson gradient-flow system in a compatible manner and ensure at the same time semi-discrete or fully-discrete total energy conservation as well as a provable entropy inequality. For certain PDE systems involutions like the divergence-free property of the magnetic field must be guaranteed.

Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

Microscopic and nonlocal interactions are common features in Biology, Social Sciences, and Materials Science, and often give rise to relevant macroscopic phenomena. The aim of the research fellowship is to develop effective models for multi-agent systems and Materials Science, starting from microscopic considerations. The research plan addresses the following three areas: (1) Multi-agent-based optimization; (2) Homogenization and Free Discontinuity; (3) Nonlocal approach to Free Discontinuity.

The research programme aims to develop physics-informed digital twins for the quantitative assessment of breast-cancer invasiveness. The activity will integrate mechanistic models of tumour growth and invasion with experimental data obtained from in vitro multicellular systems. Particular attention will be devoted to tumour–microenvironment interactions, including active wetting, tissue remodelling, adhesion, friction, traction and cell migration. The physical matematical models will be used to identify latent biomechanical parameters, such as surface tension, viscosity, active stresses, adhesion and friction properties.
